If sentiment is positive in the last 3 days and forecast is trending up, reduce late-period forecast by 1.5–2.5% to avoid overcorrection.  
If sentiment is negative in the last 3 days and forecast is trending down, increase late-period forecast by 1.5–2.5% to counteract pessimism.  
If sentiment is mixed (alternating 0.33–0.67) and forecast peaks early, reduce mid-period forecast by 0.5–1.0% to prevent overshoot.  
If sentiment is consistently low (0.00) and forecast is flat, increase early-period forecast by 0.5–1.0% to offset lack of momentum.  
If sentiment spikes to 1.00 after a dip and forecast is recovering, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% in the first 5 days to avoid premature rally.  
If sentiment is 0.00 for 3+ consecutive days and forecast is trending down, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% in the last 5 days to prevent premature collapse.
